q-43808.name: Question 1
q-43808.problem:
Given that $x,y\in {C}^{3},$ compute the standard Hermitian inner product $⟨x,y⟩$ of the following two vectors.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}i \\ 1+2i \\ -i\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}1+i \\ -1 \\ -i\end{aligned}].
$$
q-43808.worked_solution:
Using the definition of the standard Hermitian inner product, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & ={x}_{1}\overset{―}{{y}_{1}}+{x}_{2}\overset{―}{{y}_{2}}+{x}_{3}\overset{―}{{y}_{3}} \\  & =i\cdot (\overset{―}{1+i})+(1+2i)\cdot (\overset{―}{-1})+(-i)\cdot (\overset{―}{-\text{i}}) \\  & =i\cdot (1-i)+(1+2i)\cdot (-1)+(-i)\cdot \text{i} \\  & =(1+i)+(-1-2i)+1 \\  & =1-i.\end{aligned}
$$

q-43808.html:
Question 1
?

Given that x,y∈C3, compute the standard Hermitian inner product ⟨x,y⟩ of the following two vectors. x=[i1+2i−i],y=[1+i−1−i].

a
1+i
b
−1−2i
c
1−2i
d
1−i
e
−1+2i
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Using the definition of the standard Hermitian inner product, we obtain

⟨x,y⟩=x1y1―+x2y2―+x3y3―=i⋅(1+i―)+(1+2i)⋅(−1―)+(−i)⋅(−i―)=i⋅(1−i)+(1+2i)⋅(−1)+(−i)⋅i=(1+i)+(−1−2i)+1=1−i.

q-43804.name: Question 2
q-43804.problem:
Given that $x,y\in {C}^{3},$ compute the standard Hermitian inner product $⟨x,y⟩$ of the following two vectors.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}1+i \\ 2 \\ 2-i\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}1+i \\ 3 \\ 2+i\end{aligned}].
$$
q-43804.worked_solution:
Using the definition of the standard Hermitian inner product, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & ={x}_{1}\overset{―}{{y}_{1}}+{x}_{2}\overset{―}{{y}_{2}}+{x}_{3}\overset{―}{{y}_{3}} \\  & =(1+i)\cdot (\overset{―}{1+i})+2\cdot \overset{―}{3}+(2-i)(\overset{―}{2+\text{i}}) \\  & =(1+i)\cdot (1-i)+2\cdot 3+(2-i)(2-\text{i}) \\  & =2+6+(3-4\text{i}) \\  & =11-4i.\end{aligned}
$$

q-97303.name: Question 3
q-97303.problem:
Consider the standard Hermitian inner product $⟨\,\cdot \,,\,\cdot \,⟩$ over $C.$ 
Which of the following statements are true? 

- $⟨b,a⟩=\overset{―}{⟨a,b⟩}$ for any $a,b\in {C}^{n}$
- $i⟨a,b⟩=⟨-ia,b⟩$ for any  $a,b\in {C}^{n}$
- $⟨a,a⟩\in R$ for any $a\in {C}^{n}$
q-97303.worked_solution:
Recall that the standard Hermitian inner product over $C$ satisfies the following properties:

- It is linear in the first argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a+b,c⟩=⟨a,c⟩+⟨b,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨\alpha a,b⟩=\alpha ⟨a,b⟩.$

- It is antilinear in the second argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b+c⟩=⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨a,\alpha b⟩=\overset{―}{\alpha }⟨a,b⟩.$

- It has conjugate symmetry. For any $a,b\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b⟩=\overset{―}{⟨b,a⟩}.$

- It is positive-definite. For any $a\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,a⟩$ is a non-negative real number, and $⟨a,a⟩=0$ if and only if $a=0.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements. 

- Statement I is true. The inner product over $C$ has conjugate symmetry.

- Statement II is false. A complex  inner product is linear  in the first argument,  so we have 

$$
⟨-ia,b⟩=-i⟨a,b⟩\ne i⟨a,b⟩,
$$

in general.

- Statement III is true. For any $a\in {C}^{n},$  $⟨a,a⟩$ is a non-negative real number.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

q-97264.name: Question 4
q-97264.problem:
Consider the standard Hermitian inner product $⟨\,\cdot \,,\,\cdot \,⟩$ over $C.$ 
Which of the following statements are true? 

- $⟨a,b⟩=\overset{―}{⟨b,a⟩}$ for any $a,b\in {C}^{n}$
- $⟨a,\overset{―}{\alpha }b⟩=\alpha ⟨a,b⟩$ for any $a,b\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C$
- $⟨a,a⟩>0$ for any $a\in {C}^{n}$
q-97264.worked_solution:
Recall that the standard Hermitian inner product over $C$ satisfies the following properties:

- It is linear in the first argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a+b,c⟩=⟨a,c⟩+⟨b,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨\alpha a,b⟩=\alpha ⟨a,b⟩.$

- It is antilinear in the second argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b+c⟩=⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨a,\alpha b⟩=\overset{―}{\alpha }⟨a,b⟩.$

- It has conjugate symmetry. For any $a,b\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b⟩=\overset{―}{⟨b,a⟩}.$

- It is positive-definite. For any $a\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,a⟩$ is a non-negative real number, and $⟨a,a⟩=0$ if and only if $a=0.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements. 

- Statement I is true. Indeed, the inner product over $C$ has conjugate symmetry.

- Statement II is true. By the antilinearity of a complex inner product in the second argument, we have 

$$
⟨a,\overset{―}{\alpha }b⟩=\overset{―}{(\overset{―}{\alpha })}⟨a,b⟩=\alpha ⟨a,b⟩.
$$

- Statement III is false. Notice that if $a=0$ then $⟨a,a⟩=0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

q-96814.name: Question 5
q-96814.problem:
Given that $⟨\,\cdot \,,\,\cdot \,⟩$ is the standard Hermitian inner product over $C,$ find $⟨5a-2b,\,c⟩$ if 

$\,$ $⟨c,a⟩=-1+\text{i}\,$ and $\,⟨b,c⟩=3-2\text{i}.$
q-96814.worked_solution:
Recall that the inner product over $C$ satisfies the following properties. 

- It is linear in the first argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a+b,c⟩=⟨a,c⟩+⟨b,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨\alpha a,b⟩=\alpha ⟨a,b⟩.$

- It is antilinear in the second argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b+c⟩=⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨a,\alpha b⟩=\overset{―}{\alpha }⟨a,b⟩.$

- It has conjugate symmetry. For any $a,b\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b⟩=\overset{―}{⟨b,a⟩}.$

- It is positive-definite. For any $a\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,a⟩$ is a non-negative real number, and $⟨a,a⟩=0$ if and only if $a=0.$

First, we use the fact that the inner product over $C$ is linear in the first argument: 

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨5a-2b,\,c⟩ & =⟨5a,c⟩-⟨2b,c⟩ \\  & =5⟨a,c⟩-2⟨b,c⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the fact that the inner product over $C$ has conjugate symmetry: 

$$
\begin{aligned}5⟨a,c⟩-2⟨b,c⟩ & =5\overset{―}{⟨c,a⟩}-2⟨b,c⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute the values for $⟨c,a⟩$ and $⟨b,c⟩:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5\overset{―}{⟨c,a⟩}-2⟨b,c⟩ & =5(\overset{―}{-1+\text{i}})-2(3-2\text{i}) \\  & =5(-1-\text{i})-2(3-2\text{i}) \\  & =-5-5\text{i}-6+4\text{i} \\  & =-11-\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

q-96814.html:
Question 5
?

Given that ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ is the standard Hermitian inner product over C, find ⟨5a−2b,c⟩ if

⟨c,a⟩=−1+i and ⟨b,c⟩=3−2i.

a
−7+9i
b
−1−2i
c
−11−i
d
−7−i
e
−11+9i
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that the inner product over C satisfies the following properties.

  • It is linear in the first argument. For any a,b,c∈Cn and any α∈C, we have

    ⟨a+b,c⟩=⟨a,c⟩+⟨b,c⟩ and ⟨αa,b⟩=α⟨a,b⟩.

  • It is antilinear in the second argument. For any a,b,c∈Cn and any α∈C, we have

    ⟨a,b+c⟩=⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩ and ⟨a,αb⟩=α―⟨a,b⟩.

  • It has conjugate symmetry. For any a,b∈Cn, we have

    ⟨a,b⟩=⟨b,a⟩―.

  • It is positive-definite. For any a∈Cn, we have

    ⟨a,a⟩ is a non-negative real number, and ⟨a,a⟩=0 if and only if a=0.

First, we use the fact that the inner product over C is linear in the first argument:

⟨5a−2b,c⟩=⟨5a,c⟩−⟨2b,c⟩=5⟨a,c⟩−2⟨b,c⟩

Next, we use the fact that the inner product over C has conjugate symmetry:

5⟨a,c⟩−2⟨b,c⟩=5⟨c,a⟩―−2⟨b,c⟩

Finally, we substitute the values for ⟨c,a⟩ and ⟨b,c⟩:

5⟨c,a⟩―−2⟨b,c⟩=5(−1+i―)−2(3−2i)=5(−1−i)−2(3−2i)=−5−5i−6+4i=−11−i

q-97215.name: Question 6
q-97215.problem:
Given that $⟨\,\cdot \,,\,\cdot \,⟩$ is the standard Hermitian inner product over $C,$ find $⟨6a+4b,\,c⟩$ if 

$\,$ $⟨c,a⟩=2+4\text{i}\,$ and $\,⟨c,b⟩=-5-3\text{i}.$
q-97215.worked_solution:
Recall that the inner product over $C$ satisfies the following properties. 

- It is linear in the first argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a+b,c⟩=⟨a,c⟩+⟨b,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨\alpha a,b⟩=\alpha ⟨a,b⟩.$

- It is antilinear in the second argument. For any $a,b,c\in {C}^{n}$ and any $\alpha \in C,$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b+c⟩=⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩\,$ and $\,⟨a,\alpha b⟩=\overset{―}{\alpha }⟨a,b⟩.$

- It has conjugate symmetry. For any $a,b\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,b⟩=\overset{―}{⟨b,a⟩}.$

- It is positive-definite. For any $a\in {C}^{n},$ we have

$\,$ $⟨a,a⟩$ is a non-negative real number, and $⟨a,a⟩=0$ if and only if $a=0.$

First, we use the fact that the inner product over $C$ is linear in the first argument: 

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨6a+4b,\,c⟩ & =⟨6a,c⟩+⟨4b,c⟩ \\  & =6⟨a,c⟩+4⟨b,c⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the fact that the inner product over $C$ has conjugate symmetry: 

$$
\begin{aligned}6⟨a,c⟩+4⟨b,c⟩ & =6\overset{―}{⟨c,a⟩}+4\overset{―}{⟨c,b⟩}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute the values for $⟨c,a⟩$ and $⟨c,b⟩:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6\overset{―}{⟨c,a⟩}+4\overset{―}{⟨c,b⟩} & =6(\overset{―}{2+4\text{i}})+4\overset{―}{(-5-3\text{i})} \\  & =6(2-4\text{i})+4(-5+3\text{i}) \\  & =12-24\text{i}-20+12\text{i} \\  & =-8-12\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Given that ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ is the standard Hermitian inner product over C, find ⟨6a+4b,c⟩ if

⟨c,a⟩=2+4i and ⟨c,b⟩=−5−3i.

a
8+12i
b
12+8i
c
−8−12i
d
−3+i
e
3−i
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that the inner product over C satisfies the following properties.

  • It is linear in the first argument. For any a,b,c∈Cn and any α∈C, we have

    ⟨a+b,c⟩=⟨a,c⟩+⟨b,c⟩ and ⟨αa,b⟩=α⟨a,b⟩.

  • It is antilinear in the second argument. For any a,b,c∈Cn and any α∈C, we have

    ⟨a,b+c⟩=⟨a,b⟩+⟨a,c⟩ and ⟨a,αb⟩=α―⟨a,b⟩.

  • It has conjugate symmetry. For any a,b∈Cn, we have

    ⟨a,b⟩=⟨b,a⟩―.

  • It is positive-definite. For any a∈Cn, we have

    ⟨a,a⟩ is a non-negative real number, and ⟨a,a⟩=0 if and only if a=0.

First, we use the fact that the inner product over C is linear in the first argument:

⟨6a+4b,c⟩=⟨6a,c⟩+⟨4b,c⟩=6⟨a,c⟩+4⟨b,c⟩

Next, we use the fact that the inner product over C has conjugate symmetry:

6⟨a,c⟩+4⟨b,c⟩=6⟨c,a⟩―+4⟨c,b⟩―

Finally, we substitute the values for ⟨c,a⟩ and ⟨c,b⟩:

6⟨c,a⟩―+4⟨c,b⟩―=6(2+4i―)+4(−5−3i)―=6(2−4i)+4(−5+3i)=12−24i−20+12i=−8−12i
